## Overview

This script is meant to be run **one cell at a time**. First we learn how to
download data from a web API (PokéAPI, free, no account or key needed) by
starting with a single Pokémon. Then we turn that into a function, loop over many
Pokémon, save the result as a CSV, and finally run a principal component analysis (PCA).

Run each chunk in order and look at the output before moving on.

## 1. Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse) # data wrangling and plotting
library(jsonlite) # reads JSON, the format web APIs return

n_pokemon <- 1025 # 151 = Generation 1. Use 1025 for every species (slower).
```

## 2. What is an API?

An API is a web address that returns data instead of a web page. Paste this
address into your browser to see what comes back:

<https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon/1>

You will see text in JSON format. That is Bulbasaur (Pokémon number 1).
The number at the end of the address chooses the Pokémon.

## 3. Download one Pokémon

`fromJSON()` reads the web address and turns the JSON into an R list.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-one
p <- fromJSON("https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon/1")
```

Look at what we got. These are all the pieces of information available.

```{r}
#| label: look-names
names(p)
```

Simple values are easy to pull out with `$`.

```{r}
#| label: look-simple
p$name
p$height # decimetres
p$weight # hectograms
```

The base stats are tucked inside a table called `stats`.

```{r}
#| label: look-stats
p$stats
```

The stat names are nested one level deeper (`p$stats$stat$name`).
The numbers we want are in `base_stat`.

```{r}
#| label: look-stats-2
p$stats$stat$name
p$stats$base_stat
```

Types work the same way.

```{r}
#| label: look-types
p$types$type$name
```

## 4. Pull out the pieces we want

Combine the stat names and values into one named vector.

```{r}
#| label: stats-vector
stats <- setNames(p$stats$base_stat, p$stats$stat$name)
stats
```

Now build a one-row table (a tibble) for this Pokémon.

```{r}
#| label: one-row
types <- p$types$type$name

tibble(
  id = p$id,
  name = p$name,
  type1 = types[1],
  type2 = if (length(types) > 1) types[2] else NA_character_,
  height_m = p$height / 10, # convert to metres
  weight_kg = p$weight / 10, # convert to kilograms
  hp = stats[["hp"]],
  attack = stats[["attack"]],
  defense = stats[["defense"]],
  sp_attack = stats[["special-attack"]],
  sp_defense = stats[["special-defense"]],
  speed = stats[["speed"]]
)
```

## 5. Some information lives at a different address

Whether a Pokémon is legendary is stored in a second endpoint,
`pokemon-species`. We fetch it the same way.

```{r}
#| label: species
s <- fromJSON("https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon-species/1")

s$generation$name
s$is_legendary
s$is_mythical
```

## 6. Wrap it in a function

Everything we just did, bundled so we can reuse it for any Pokémon number.

```{r}
#| label: function
get_pokemon <- function(id) {
  p <- fromJSON(paste0("https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon/", id))
  s <- fromJSON(paste0("https://pokeapi.co/api/v2/pokemon-species/", id))

  stats <- setNames(p$stats$base_stat, p$stats$stat$name)
  types <- p$types$type$name

  Sys.sleep(0.1) # short pause so we are polite to the free server

  tibble(
    id = p$id,
    name = p$name,
    type1 = types[1],
    type2 = if (length(types) > 1) types[2] else NA_character_,
    height_m = p$height / 10,
    weight_kg = p$weight / 10,
    hp = stats[["hp"]],
    attack = stats[["attack"]],
    defense = stats[["defense"]],
    sp_attack = stats[["special-attack"]],
    sp_defense = stats[["special-defense"]],
    speed = stats[["speed"]],
    generation = s$generation$name,
    is_legendary = s$is_legendary,
    is_mythical = s$is_mythical
  )
}
```

Test it on Pikachu (number 25).

```{r}
#| label: test-function
get_pokemon(25)
```

## 7. Download a few at once

`map()` runs the function on each number, and `list_rbind()` stacks the results
into one table.

```{r}
#| label: download-few
few <- map(1:5, get_pokemon) |> list_rbind()
few
```

## 8. Download them all and save a CSV

Downloading hundreds of Pokémon means hundreds of web requests, so we only do it
once and save the result. `possibly()` keeps the loop going if one request fails.
This cell takes a minute or two.

```{r}
#| label: download-all
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
cache_file <- file.path("data", paste0("pokemon_", n_pokemon, ".csv"))

if (!file.exists(cache_file)) {
  safe_get <- possibly(get_pokemon, otherwise = NULL)

  pokemon <- map(seq_len(n_pokemon), safe_get, .progress = TRUE) |>
    list_rbind()

  write_csv(pokemon, cache_file)
}
```

From now on we read the saved file instead of downloading again.

```{r}
#| label: read-cache
pokemon <- read_csv(cache_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
write_csv(pokemon, "pokemon 151.csv")
glimpse(pokemon)
```

## 9. Explore

```{r}
#| label: explore
stat_cols <- c("hp", "attack", "defense", "sp_attack", "sp_defense", "speed")

pokemon |>
  select(all_of(stat_cols)) |>
  summary()
```

Which stats move together?

```{r}
#| label: correlations
pokemon |>
  select(all_of(stat_cols)) |>
  cor() |>
  round(2)
```

## 10. Run the PCA

We center and scale the stats so no stat dominates just because its numbers
are bigger.

```{r}
#| label: pca
pca <- prcomp(pokemon[, stat_cols], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
summary(pca)
```

### Scree plot

How much variation does each component capture?

```{r}
#| label: scree
var_tbl <- tibble(
  PC = paste0("PC", seq_along(pca$sdev)),
  prop_var = pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)
)

ggplot(var_tbl, aes(PC, prop_var)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::percent(prop_var, accuracy = 0.1)),
    vjust = -0.4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance explained", title = "Scree plot") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Loadings

Loadings show which stats drive each component. PC1 is usually an "overall
strength" axis. Later components contrast things like speed versus defense.

```{r}
#| label: loadings
round(pca$rotation[, 1:3], 2)
```

## 11. Plot the Pokémon in PC space

```{r}
#| label: scores
scores <- bind_cols(pokemon, as_tibble(pca$x[, 1:3]))

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, color = is_legendary)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("grey60", "firebrick"),
    labels = c("Not legendary", "Legendary"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Pokémon in PCA space",
    subtitle = "Colored by legendary status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Label the extreme Pokémon. This needs the `ggrepel` package
(`install.packages("ggrepel")` if you do not have it).

```{r}
#| label: extremes
extremes <- scores |>
  filter(
    abs(PC1) > quantile(abs(PC1), 0.97) | abs(PC2) > quantile(abs(PC2), 0.97)
  )

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(data = extremes, color = "firebrick") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = extremes,
    aes(label = name),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = 30
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

A biplot adds arrows showing how each stat points through the plot.

```{r}
#| label: biplot
arrows <- as_tibble(pca$rotation[, 1:2], rownames = "stat") |>
  mutate(across(c(PC1, PC2), ~ .x * 4)) # stretch arrows so they are visible

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = type1), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(
    data = arrows,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = arrows,
    aes(PC1, PC2, label = stat),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  labs(color = "Primary type") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Things to try

1. Add `height_m` and `weight_kg` (log-transformed) to the PCA. How do the loadings change?
2. Does PC1 separate legendary from non-legendary Pokémon? Compare mean PC1 by group.
3. Cluster the PC1 and PC2 scores with `kmeans()`. Do the clusters match types?
4. Set `n_pokemon <- 1025` and compare generations.
5. Subset to a list of Pokémon you care about (for example a current competitive
   roster) and see whether they separate from the rest in PC space.
